subject: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>, Sam Patel <sam@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 26, 2027 at 3:02 PM PDT
Subject: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the logging and PII redaction items we discussed.

Recap (high-level):
- Scope: request/response logs, selected headers, trace/correlation IDs, and structured event logs from the inference path.
- Goals: ensure PII (SSNs, full card numbers, customer-identifiable addresses) are never stored in plaintext in logs; preserve enough correlation metadata for debugging; meet FintechCo retention/residency requirements.
- Constraints you mentioned: 90-day retention, US-only data residency, need to keep trace IDs for debug but only in hashed/tokenized form, and last4 of card allowed for reconciliation but not full PAN.

What Redwood can provide (summary):
- Per-customer logging controls: enable/disable request/response logging at route level.
- Redaction rules engine: configurable rules to remove or mask fields by JSON path or regex (examples: card_number -> mask, ssn -> drop).
- Header masking: configurable header allowlist/denylist (we typically strip Authorization and cookies by default).
- Trace ID handling: HMAC-hashed trace IDs (per-tenant salt) so IDs are stable for correlation but not reversible from logs; option for reversible tokenization only in Private deployments under customer KMS.
- Retention & deletion: TTL-based log retention and on-demand purge APIs; export hooks to your SIEM for archival before purge.
- Deployments: Hosted with US-only regions + Dedicated/Private for stronger residency/KMS controls.

Attachments: I attached a short overview deck of our logging controls (redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf) and a suggested redaction-rule template we can fill together.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You to share the FintechCo logging requirements doc and any sample log/event schema (if available).
2) Rishi/Vivek from our infra team to do a technical sync (30\u201345m) to walk through redaction rules and trace handling.
3) We\u2019ll produce a proposed redaction rule set and a short test plan for you to validate.

Proposed times for the tech sync (PDT): Mon Jun 28 10:00\u201310:45, Mon Jun 28 14:00\u201314:45, Tue Jun 29 09:00\u201309:45. Let me know what works.

Thanks — happy to prioritize this.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 26, 2027 at 4:33 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — great summary. Attaching our internal Logging Requirements v1.2 (FintechCo-Logging-Requirements-v1.2.pdf). A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: default 90 days for logs generated by inference endpoints. Longer retention only for aggregated metrics exported to our analytics cluster.
- PII: SSNs and full PANs must never be present in logs. Last4 is OK. Customer name and email are considered PII in our policy and should be redacted unless explicitly required for a workflow; prefer tokenization.
- Trace IDs: we need stable correlation IDs across services for triage, but they must be non-reversible. Hashing with a per-customer salt sounds acceptable — we can provide the salt via a secure channel.
- Headers: please strip Authorization and cookie headers in logs; retain X-Request-ID (after hashing) and X-Service-Version.

We\u2019ll share a sample event schema (JSON) by end of day Monday.

Also — would like to include our security lead on the tech sync: Karen Lee (karen.lee@fintechco.com). Can she join?

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FintechCo

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction - post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks for the doc and for looping in Karen. Monday EOD for the sample schema works; we\u2019ll review as soon as it\u2019s up.

Quick follow-up answers to the items you raised:
- Hashing trace IDs: we will implement HMAC hashing with a per-tenant salt; the hashed ID will be stable and cannot be reversed from logs. For the Hosted/Standard offering we can accept a salt via secure upload and store it encrypted at rest. For Private deployments we can also integrate with customer KMS for additional controls.
- Tokenization vs masking: our redaction engine supports both masking (e.g., show last4) and full removal. We\u2019ll map rules to JSON paths you provide and run a small batch test on a sample payload.
- Headers: default strip list includes Authorization and Cookie; we will whitelist X-Service-Version and include X-Request-ID only in hashed form as discussed.

Action items I\u2019m taking:
- Rishi and Vivek will prepare a draft redaction-rule CSV based on your schema. (Rishi: please use the template attached.)
- We\u2019ll schedule a 30\u201345m tech sync with Karen + your security team. Proposed slots: Mon Jun 28 10:00\u201310:45 PDT or Mon Jun 28 14:00\u201314:45 PDT.

If those work I\u2019ll send a calendar invite with a brief agenda and the sandbox test plan.

—
Marissa

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction - post-call recap & next steps

Looping in a few technical notes and proposed on-boarding steps from infra:

1) Please ask FintechCo to share: a sample JSON event schema, a small set (~20) of anonymized example events (with PII redacted) and the explicit list of fields they consider PII.
2) I\u2019ve started a draft redaction-rule-template.csv that maps JSON path -> rule (mask/drop/hash) -> example. I\u2019ve attached the CSV to this thread.
3) For hashing trace IDs we\u2019ll use HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant salt; we\u2019ll store salts encrypted (hosted) and support KMS-backed secrets for Dedicated/Private. We won\u2019t store raw salts in plaintext.
4) Test plan: we\u2019ll run a masked logging mode in a sandbox for a 24h window, then provide output samples for FintechCo to validate. If everything looks good we\u2019ll enable on a per-route basis in staged traffic.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
